## Exercise

Look again at the data of a dispersing white tail deer that we discussed in the code walkthrough and try to create a similar analysis and plot for the turn-angle distribution. 

Use a von Mises distribution for turn angles.

## Solution 

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show solution"
#| eval: FALSE

library(amt)
library(tidyverse)


# Load the data
dat <- read_csv(here::here("data/moll_et_al2021.csv"))


# Parse date
dat$t <- mdy_hm(dat$t, tz = "America/Chicago") # This important!

dat <- filter(dat, t >= ymd("2017-11-04"), t <= ymd("2017-11-24"))
trk <- make_track(dat, x, y, t, crs = 4326)
trk1 <- trk |> track_resample(rate = minutes(90), tolerance = minutes(10))

trk1 <- trk1 |> transform_coords(32515)

steps <- trk1 |> steps_by_burst() |> # Steps
  time_of_day(where = "both") # Add time of day

# Fitting statistical distributions ----

# Next we can fit a gamma distribution to the steps
# Day
day <- fit_distr(
  steps |> filter(tod_start_ == "day") |> pull(ta_),
  "vonmises"
)

night <- fit_distr(
  steps |> filter(tod_start_ == "night") |> pull(ta_),
  "vonmises"
)

day$params
night$params

res <- tibble(
  when = c("day", "night"),
  what = c("kappa", "kappa"),
  est = c(day$params$kappa, night$params$kappa),
  se = sqrt(
    c(day$vcov, night$vcov)
  )
)


td <- res |> nest(-when) |>
  mutate(vm = map(data, ~ {
    tibble(
      x = seq(-3, 3, len = 250),
      y = dvonmises(x, mu = 0, kappa = .x$est)
    )
  })) |>
  select(tod_start_ = when, vm) |>
  unnest(cols = vm)

# Plotting
steps |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ta_)) +
  geom_density() +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y), data = td, col = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ tod_start_)


# ... Derived quantities ----
# Expected speed
res |> filter(when == "day") |> pull(est) 
res |> filter(when == "night") |> pull(est) 

res


res |>
  ggplot(aes(x = when, y = est, ymin = est - 1.96 * se, ymax = est + 1.96 * se)) +
  geom_pointrange()



```
